title: NimbusPay - SDK quickstart, auth & Optimize walkthrough
summary: Overview and hands-on walkthrough of Redwood SDKs (Python + TS), environment setup, API keys vs SSO, and Optimize suggestions for latency/cost tradeoffs. Agreed to run a 2-week pilot with sandbox keys and a small eval prompt set.
topics: Auth patterns: API keys, SSO, KMS for private deploys
Redwood Optimize recommendations: batching, quantization, caching
action_items: Jordan Patel: Share sandbox repo + sample prompts (due 2025-08-23)
Maya Chen: Provide Optimize tuning checklist and recommended quantization profiles (due 2025-08-26)
Alex Rivera: Confirm pilot dataset and internal stakeholders (due 2025-08-25)
next_steps: Start 2-week pilot with dedicated sandbox keys
Schedule SE-led benchmark session (30-45 mins) next week
Customer to provide SLA/latency targets and token budget
transcript:
[00:00:00] Jordan Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan, AE at Redwood. Quick roll call?
[00:00:10] Alex Rivera: Alex here, engineering. Priya is on, Marcus in product, and Eli... Eli's listening.
[00:00:20] Maya Chen: Hi all, Maya, I'm the solutions SE, I'll lead the SDK walkthrough.
[00:00:30] Priya Shah: Priya, SRE, quick note: we care about data residency and KMS integration.
[00:00:45] Jordan Patel: Great, we'll cover both. Agenda: quickstart for Python/TS SDK, auth options, then Optimize recommendations.
[00:01:12] Marcus Li: We probably have 40-60ms P95 target for short prompts, and a cost envelope.
[00:01:25] Maya Chen: Understood. We'll show hosted API but also note Dedicated and Private options for strict residency.
[00:01:38] Speaker 1: (mumble)
[00:02:05] Maya Chen: Alright, jumping in. First the SDK: pip install redwood-inference, npm i @redwood/inference, minimal code samples in the repo I linked in the invite.
[00:02:25] Alex Rivera: Can you show env var patterns? We use multiple clusters and CI so secrets rotation is important.
[00:02:40] Maya Chen: Sure, two main patterns: API keys via REDWOOD_API_KEY for quickstarts, and SSO/SAML for console access. For CI we recommend vaults or cloud KMS; we have examples for AWS KMS and GCP KMS.
[00:03:10] Priya Shah: When you say KMS, is that for customer-managed keys or just key wrapping? We need customer-managed CMKs that never leave our account.
[00:03:25] Maya Chen: Good question. For Redwood Private we support customer-managed keys (CMKs) where the HSM/KMS is in your account; hosted can integrate via envelope encryption with keys you control. There's sometimes a small metadata handshake that gets logged but payloads are never stored unencrypted.
[00:03:50] Jordan Patel: I'll attach the SOC2/ISO docs in the follow-up.
[00:04:10] Marcus Li: Walk us through a simple Python sample?
[00:04:24] Maya Chen: Absolutely. (screen share) Example:
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
resp = client.generate("Summarize customer support tickets")
print(resp.text)
[00:04:45] Maya Chen: That's the simplest flow. For streaming: client.stream_generate(...) and we show how to hook into webhooks or SSE.
[00:05:05] Alex Rivera: Any code for batching? We expect spikes with our payment flow and want to amortize cost.
[00:05:20] Maya Chen: SDK exposes a BatchClient that can group similar prompt shapes. Also Redwood Optimize will suggest batch sizes based on your latency SLOs and token distribution. We'll share a CSV of your token histogram template.
[00:05:48] Alex Rivera: Is batching automatic in Hosted? Or do we need to implement in-app?
[00:06:00] Maya Chen: The serving runtime does continuous batching automatically on the server-side, but client-side batching reduces scheduling overhead for many small prompts. So we recommend a hybrid: let the runtime batch, but if you have many micro-requests, use the BatchClient to structure them.
[00:06:25] Priya Shah: What about KV cache? We have context reuse in chat sessions.
[00:06:40] Maya Chen: We support prefix/KV caching. For chat, you can pin the KV cache when you rehydrate sessions; in Dedicated or Private you can opt for in-memory caches tied to instance groups to reduce token costs.
[00:07:05] Speaker 2: 
[00:07:20] Jordan Patel: Quick note on model selection: you can route by policy—latency vs cost—so for lower cost we can serve a quantized variant; for high-quality we route to full-precision.
[00:07:45] Marcus Li: That sounds like we can degrade gracefully if capacity is tight?
[00:07:55] Maya Chen: Exactly. Automatic fallback to compatible model variants, and you can set canary rollouts.
[00:08:10] Alex Rivera: Show me the TypeScript example.
[00:08:20] Maya Chen: (switching) import { Redwood } from '@redwood/inference';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
const out = await client.generate({ prompt: '...' });
console.log(out.text);
[00:08:45] Maya Chen: We also have typed responses for function calling and structured JSON output; the TS types are included in the package.
[00:09:10] Priya Shah: For our CI, we need to rotate keys every 7 days and have short-lived tokens. Do you support ephemeral tokens?
[00:09:25] Maya Chen: Yes, short-lived tokens via the Console with role-based grants or via our token exchange endpoints. We also support temporary service tokens that your infra can mint using a short-lived signed assertion.
[00:09:50] Alex Rivera: How do we audit usage? We need per-team token-level cost attribution.
[00:10:05] Jordan Patel: Redwood Console has per-token cost breakdowns, route-level dashboards, and you can export CSVs for chargeback. Also trace hooks for individual requests.
[00:10:30] Marcus Li: Are there SDKs for batch ingestion of embeddings? We plan to embed transaction metadata for search.
[00:10:45] Maya Chen: Yes, embeddings client supports bulk upsert operations and recommended chunk sizes. Optimize will suggest quantized models for embeddings to save cost without big quality loss.
[00:11:10] Priya Shah: Security: do you provide audit logs for key operations and access?
[00:11:25] Maya Chen: Audit logs are available for Console actions, key rotations, and model deployments. For Private deployments, logs are stored in your SIEM if you opt-in.
[00:11:50] Alex Rivera: Ok, let's talk Optimize: how does it recommend batch sizes and quantization?
[00:12:05] Maya Chen: Optimize analyzes token distribution, latency SLOs, and hardware targets. It outputs suggested batch target, cache TTLs, and which quantization profile to use (8-bit, 4-bit, mixed). The suggestions are workload-specific.
[00:12:30] Marcus Li: Does Optimize run on our data or synthetic traces? We can't upload production customer texts.
[00:12:45] Maya Chen: You can run Optimize on synthetic traces or an anonymized prompt set. We have a local eval harness so you can run analyses without sending raw content to Redwood—especially for Private deployments.
[00:13:10] Speaker 3: (crosstalk)
[00:13:25] Maya Chen: For latency-critical flows, we recommend smaller batch targets and pinning to Dedicated capacity with burst pools. For lower-priority background jobs, increase batching and use quantized variants.
[00:13:50] Alex Rivera: Any benchmarks for 2k token sequences on an A100 equivalent?
[00:14:02] Maya Chen: Our published benchmark shows ~120ms per token on throughput-optimized instances for certain models; I'll attach model-specific CSVs. For your 2k workload we should run a short benchmark—want to do that in the pilot.
[00:14:25] Jordan Patel: I'll coordinate the benchmark.
[00:14:35] Priya Shah: Regarding data residency — we need EU-only processing. How does Redwood handle region pinning?
[00:14:48] Maya Chen: You can set region policy to EU-only; for Private you can deploy on premises or VPC in your preferred cloud region. Hosted accounts can be region pinned with data guarantees and audit proofs.
[00:15:12] Alex Rivera: Pricing question: how do minibatches affect cost? Is it per-token always, or are there amortized charges?
[00:15:25] Jordan Patel: Billing is per-token, but Optimize and caching reduce number of billed tokens by prefix-KV reuse. Also batch efficiency can reduce per-token compute cost and sometimes results in lower unit price for reserved capacity. We'll include cost estimates in the follow-up.
[00:15:55] Marcus Li: Who do we talk to about enterprise SLAs?
[00:16:05] Jordan Patel: I'll loop in our sales engineer and enterprise lead—Lena is on the invite and can own SLA discussion.
[00:16:20] Maya Chen: Quick demo of Console: (navigates) You can create API keys, configure role-based access, and view Optimize suggestions under the 'Workloads' tab.
[00:16:50] Alex Rivera: Can we automate key creation via API?
[00:16:58] Maya Chen: Yes, keys can be created via the admin API with scoped permissions.
[00:17:20] Priya Shah: Any gotchas with containerized apps that spawn many short-lived processes?
[00:17:35] Maya Chen: Yes, if each process holds a connection it can create too many concurrent requests. We recommend a shared client process or connection pool approach. Also short-lived tokens help limit blast radius.
[00:17:58] Jordan Patel: We're nearing halfway, want to pivot to pilot scoping?
[00:18:08] Alex Rivera: Yes—pilot goals: validate latency P95 ~<80ms for 256-token prompts, cost per 1k tokens < $0.75 (ballpark), and ensure SSO + KMS integration.
[00:18:25] Maya Chen: Proposed pilot: 2 weeks, sandbox keys, run two benchmarks (small prompts, large prompts), and a functional test for chat KV caching. We'll provide the harness.
[00:18:48] Marcus Li: What level of support during pilot? On-call SE?
[00:18:58] Jordan Patel: We'll provide SE office hours twice during the pilot, and Slack channel for logs.
[00:19:15] Priya Shah: Can we get sample Terraform for Private on-prem deployment?
[00:19:25] Maya Chen: Yes, we have a starter repo for Private and VPC networking—I'll share link.
[00:19:40] Alex Rivera: Any restrictions on PII in prompts? We prefer tokenization on-prem.
[00:19:52] Maya Chen: For hosted, we recommend redaction or use Private deployment. For PCI-sensitive flows, Private is typical.
[00:20:10] Speaker 4: 
[00:20:25] Jordan Patel: Let's recap real quick—Jordan: send pricing and pilot worksheet; Maya: send SDK samples and Optimize checklist; Alex: share pilot dataset and acceptance tests.
[00:20:45] Alex Rivera: Sounds good. A couple final quick questions: do you support model fine-tuning or just instruction-tuning/adapter layers?
[00:20:58] Maya Chen: We support both instruction-tuning and adapters; full fine-tuning is offered on Dedicated contracts. For hosted, we recommend adapters or prompt engineering and eval harness.
[00:21:20] Marcus Li: How about rollout strategy—can we do canary by tenant?
[00:21:32] Maya Chen: Yes, canary rollouts by route or tenant with automatic fallback policies.
[00:21:50] Priya Shah: One more: SLAs—what does your uptime SLA look like for Dedicated?
[00:21:58] Jordan Patel: Dedicated comes with SLA options; typical is 99.9%+ with page support. We'll include exact terms.
[00:22:15] Maya Chen: I'll attach the Dedicated spec sheet.
[00:22:35] Alex Rivera: Great, thanks.
[00:22:45] Jordan Patel: Thanks everyone—closing notes: we'll send artifacts by EOD and schedule the benchmark.
[00:23:05] (meeting ends early; silence)

Notes: Transcript contains minor mis-hearings, some speaker attribution generic. Shared links referenced during meeting: sandbox repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/nimbuspay-sandbox, Optimize checklist doc: https://redwood.ai/docs/optimize-checklist (internal link).
